system_description.narrative_title: Russian military escalation and global geopolitical ripple effects
system_description.narrative_summary: A concentrated surge in Russian air, missile and drone strikes against Ukraine — paired with strikes on infrastructure, economic targets and cross-border incidents — is driving heightened NATO preparedness, allied intelligence-sharing, sanctions and diplomatic manoeuvres (including a possible Putin-Trump meeting at the G20). The system is open: kinetic operations, economic shocks (energy, trade), information/cyber actions and diplomatic signals flow bidirectionally, producing feedback loops that can amplify escalation (military reprisals, broader sanctions, alliance shifts) or enable de-escalation via talks and summit diplomacy.
system_description.scope: The Russia–Ukraine military campaign and its immediate geopolitical consequences: military strikes and counterstrikes, cross-border incidents, NATO and allied military and intelligence responses, sanctions and economic impacts (energy, trade), and high-level diplomatic engagements (G20, US–Russia talks).
system_description.super_system: The global international security and geopolitical order
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and commodity markets (energy security, food/wheat supply)
Regional conflicts and humanitarian crises (Horn of Africa, Sudan, Congo)
evidence_headlines: Russia hits Kyiv with ballistic missiles, drones, killing two
Russia’s new air campaign seeks to destroy Ukrainian economy
Russia could attack Nato country within months, Denmark warns
US invites Putin to G-20 Summit at Trump Resort in Florida
NATO steps up intelligence-sharing over Russia threat, top commander says
Ukraine hits Moscow with ‘largest ever’ drone attack

variables.name: Kinetic operation intensity
variables.description: Measures the aggregated rate and intensity of armed strikes, maneuvers and direct kinetic engagements across the theatre.

variables.name: Cross-border incident rate
variables.description: Measures the frequency and severity of military or hostile incidents that cross or threaten to cross recognized borders.

variables.name: Allied military readiness
variables.description: Measures the aggregated readiness of partner forces, including mobilization levels, troop posture and rapid-response capacity.

variables.name: Intelligence-sharing rate
variables.description: Measures the volume, timeliness and integration of shared intelligence and situational data among partners.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure level
variables.description: Measures the cumulative economic, financial and regulatory pressure applied through punitive measures and restrictions.

variables.name: Energy supply disruption level
variables.description: Measures the degree to which energy production, transport and deliveries are interrupted or constrained.

variables.name: Critical infrastructure damage
variables.description: Measures the stock of physical damage to transport, industrial, energy and communications infrastructure affecting functionality.

variables.name: Cyber operation activity
variables.description: Measures the frequency, scale and disruptive effect of offensive and defensive cyber operations targeting infrastructure and information systems.

variables.name: Information-warfare intensity
variables.description: Measures the intensity and reach of coordinated messaging, disinformation, propaganda and information-denial operations.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: Measures the rate and scale of formal and informal diplomatic interactions, negotiations, and high-level signaling.

variables.name: Political willingness to de-escalate
variables.description: Measures the degree of expressed and credible intent among political actors to reduce tensions and pursue negotiated solutions.

variables.name: Defense logistics capacity
variables.description: Measures the stock capacity of logistics, munitions, repair, transport and sustainment that supports prolonged military operations.

variables.name: Global trade disruption magnitude
variables.description: Measures the extent to which international trade flows, supply chains and commerce are delayed, rerouted or reduced.

variables.name: Public risk perception
variables.description: Measures population-level perceptions of personal, economic and national security risk driven by conflict and related shocks.

variables.name: Escalation feedback strength
variables.description: Measures the propensity of actions and reactions in the system to produce reinforcing cycles that amplify conflict and retaliation.

variables.name: Allied political cohesion
variables.description: Measures the degree of policy alignment, burden-sharing and coordinated decision-making among partner actors.

catalysts.title: Possible Putin–Trump G20/bilateral in December
catalysts.description: A Putin attendance or bilateral meeting with Trump at the G20 in December could shift high‑level diplomatic signalling and de‑/re‑escalation dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: US invites Putin to G20; Russia undecided; possible Trump summit. (headlines: U.S. invites Putin to G-20; Russia hasn't decided)

catalysts.title: Proposed US–Russia–Ukraine trilateral meeting (UAE)
catalysts.description: A proposed trilateral meeting in the UAE between US, Russia and Ukraine could create negotiation channels and alter sanction and de‑escalation trajectories.
catalysts.rationale: US proposes trilateral meeting in UAE; Kremlin says meeting may happen soon. (headlines: US proposes trilateral meeting; Kremlin says meeting may happen soon)

catalysts.title: Intensified Russian missile/drone air campaign
catalysts.description: Sustained, higher‑intensity Russian missile and drone strikes targeting cities, industry and energy assets will amplify kinetic and infrastructure impacts.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: ballistic missiles, drones hit Kyiv; new air campaign aims to destroy Ukrainian economy; strikes on refineries/data centres.

catalysts.title: NATO intelligence‑sharing ramp‑up
catalysts.description: Accelerated NATO intelligence sharing and coordination increases situational awareness and adjusts allied readiness and posture in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: NATO steps up intelligence‑sharing; US to provide critical capabilities (top commander statements).

catalysts.title: U.S. meets Ukraine assistance deadline
catalysts.description: The Trump administration meeting a stated Ukraine assistance deadline will boost logistics and sustainment flows for Ukrainian forces.
catalysts.rationale: Exclusive: Trump administration to meet Ukraine assistance deadline (headline).

catalysts.title: Energy‑truce negotiations and winter disruption risk
catalysts.description: Negotiations over energy arrangements and winter seasonal pressures could determine widespread supply disruptions and economic spillovers.
catalysts.rationale: Zelenskiy warns of painful winter if energy truce talks fail; Black Sea/energy disruptions and refinery attacks reported.

catalysts.title: Elevated cyber operations targeting Ukrainian infrastructure
catalysts.description: Ongoing cyber attacks on data centres and telecoms will increase digital disruption, infrastructure damage and information‑shock effects.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Russia targets Ukraine’s data centres; telecoms disrupted in Tigray; drone and infrastructure strikes reported.

catalysts.title: EU decision to lift sanctions on two Russian oligarchs
catalysts.description: An EU decision to lift select oligarch sanctions will modestly alter the sanctions landscape and provoke allied political reactions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: EU to lift sanctions on two Russian oligarchs.
